statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the entries of r are exactly the valid starting positions, each appearing exactly once, in any order. An integer i is a valid starting position exactly when: 0 <= i; i + L <= len(s); and there exists a permutation p of the index set {0,...,m-1} (a bijection from this set to itself) such that for every j with 0 <= j < m and every k with 0 <= k < wl, s[i + j*wl + k] = words[p[j]][k]. Equivalently, the m consecutive length-wl byte blocks of s[i .. i+L) have the same multiset as the entries of words. The entries of r are exactly the integers i satisfying this definition, each exactly once, and r contains no other integers.
preconditions: Let m = len(words), wl = len(words[0]), and L = m*wl. Assume the problem constraints: 1 <= len(s) <= 10000; 1 <= m <= 5000; 1 <= wl <= 30; for every j with 0 <= j < m, len(words[j]) = wl; s and all words[j] are ASCII lowercase byte arrays.

statement: For every s and words satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, overflow, or panic.
